_comment: WorldQuant Brain simulation mechanics — sourced from Brain public docs, tutorials, and practitioner guides. Each field is annotated: 'confirmed' = from official Brain documentation; 'inferred' = derived from practitioner experience and public forum posts.

overview.description: Brain runs a fully vectorized daily equity backtest. For each trading day, it evaluates your expression once for every stock in the universe, producing a cross-sectional vector of numeric scores. These scores are processed through a standardized pipeline (neutralization → decay → truncation → sizing) to produce dollar weights, then P&L is computed from next-day returns.

TOP3000.description: ~3000 most liquid US equities, roughly corresponding to Russell 3000
TOP3000.selection_basis: trailing average daily dollar volume (price × volume), rebalanced periodically

TOP1000.description: Top 1000 most liquid US equities, roughly S&P 500 + mid-caps

TOP200.description: Top 200 most liquid US equities (large-cap only)

universe.rebalance_note: Universe membership changes daily based on trailing liquidity. Survivorship bias is avoided: stocks that were in the universe historically remain in the backtest even if they were later delisted.
universe.impact_on_signals: Narrower universes (TOP500) have fewer stocks — signals need higher per-stock weights to hit non-trivial turnover. Fundamental signals work best in TOP1000 (better data coverage). Reversal signals work well in TOP3000 (more microstructure noise to exploit).

position_sizing.book_description: $20M long + $20M short = $40M gross exposure. Dollar-neutral by construction.
position_sizing.normalization: After truncation, weights are re-normalized so the long book sums to $20M and short book sums to -$20M.

pipeline_order.description: Brain applies transformations in this exact order each day:
steps: 1. EVALUATE expression → raw cross-sectional vector (one scalar per stock)
2. PASTEURIZE → replace NaN/Inf with 0; suppress stocks with insufficient data history
4. TRUNCATE → cap each stock's |weight| at truncation × total_book
5. DECAY → exponential smoothing with previous days' positions
6. NORMALIZE → scale so long book = $20M, short book = $20M
7. COMPUTE P&L → apply next-day returns to positions
pipeline_order.critical_note: Decay is applied AFTER neutralization and truncation — it smooths positions over time, not the raw signal. This is why increasing decay reduces turnover: it blends today's position with yesterday's, reducing daily rebalancing.

neutralization.formula: neutralized_i = signal_i - mean(signal_j for j in same_group)
neutralization.method: Equal-weighted subtraction of group mean. NOT market-cap weighted.

groups.Market: Entire universe is one group. Equivalent to dollar-neutral (long=short book).
groups.Sector: GICS sector (11 sectors: Energy, Materials, Industrials, etc.)
groups.Subindustry: GICS subindustry (~160 groups). Tightest neutralization; removes most sector beta.

impact.Market: Removes broad market beta. Long = short in dollar terms.
impact.Subindustry: Removes sector, industry, AND subindustry beta. Alpha is purely stock-specific. Turnover tends to be higher because group means change daily.

neutralization.double_neutralization_warning: If your expression already calls group_neutralize(x, sector) internally, set neutralization=Market in settings. Setting neutralization=Subindustry ON TOP of an internal group_neutralize creates double-demeaning, distorting positions.

decay.description: Exponential moving average of daily positions. Weight of most recent day = 1/(d+1). Each prior day's contribution decays by factor d/(d+1).

0.use_case: No smoothing — position equals today's raw signal. Only for very low-turnover fundamentals.

4.use_case: Fast signals — reversal, microstructure, short-window technical. Typical turnover 30–60%.

6.use_case: Medium signals — volatility, earnings event, analyst. Typical turnover 15–40%.

8.use_case: Slow signals — fundamental ratios, quality factors. Typical turnover 8–25%.

10.use_case: Very slow signals — long-window fundamentals. Typical turnover 5–18%.

decay.turnover_rule_of_thumb: Higher decay → lower turnover for the same underlying signal. If turnover is too high (>70%), increase decay by 2-4. If too low (<5%), decrease decay toward 0.

truncation.description: Each stock's weight (as a fraction of the total long or short book) is capped at the truncation value. After capping, weights are re-normalized.

parameter_guide.0.01: Highly diversified — effectively 100+ stocks with material weight. Good for fundamental signals with many constituents.
parameter_guide.0.05: Balanced default — ~20–50 stocks with material weight. Works for most archetypes.
parameter_guide.0.10: Concentrated — ~10–20 stocks. Appropriate for TOP200 universe or very high-conviction signals.

truncation.concentrated_weight_check: If truncation is too loose (large), Brain may flag CONCENTRATED_WEIGHT: top few stocks represent too much of the book. Lower truncation (e.g., from 0.10 to 0.05) to fix.

pasteurization.behavior: Replaces NaN, Inf, and extremely stale values with 0 in the position vector before neutralization. Ensures stocks with missing data don't distort group means or positions.
pasteurization.when_matters: Fields with low coverage (<80%) will have many NaN stocks. Pasteurization zeros those out rather than propagating NaN through the pipeline.

unit_handling.behavior: Brain checks that branches of if_else, min, max, abs are unit-consistent. E.g., mixing price (USD) with unitless rank() triggers a UNITS warning and the alpha cannot be submitted.
unit_handling.fix: Normalize all branches to the same unit before combining: divide price fields by ts_mean(price, N) to get a ratio; use rank() or zscore() to make everything unitless.

components.Sharpe: Annualized Sharpe ratio = mean(daily_pnl) / std(daily_pnl) * sqrt(252)
components.AnnualizedReturn: Annualized portfolio return as a decimal (e.g., 0.08 = 8%)
components.0.125_floor: Prevents infinite fitness from near-static portfolios. Turnover below 12.5% is treated as 12.5% for this formula.

fitness_formula.intuition: Fitness rewards Sharpe AND penalizes high turnover. A Sharpe=2 alpha with 60% turnover scores lower than Sharpe=1.5 with 15% turnover. Turnover ≈ proxy for transaction costs. The sqrt compression means returns need to 4× to offset 16× turnover.

returns.note: Not a primary gate but enters fitness formula

turnover.formula: mean(sum(|weight_t - weight_{t-1}|) / total_book_value) over all days
turnover.reported_as: Percentage (e.g., 40.0 for 40%). Brain API returns as decimal [0,1] — multiply by 100.
turnover.target_range: 1% to 70% for submission. Below 1% = static/trivial. Above 70% = too costly.

drawdown.description: Maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of cumulative P&L

margin.description: Average daily profit per unit of turnover. Higher is better.

in_sample_out_of_sample.description: Brain evaluates every alpha on both IS (historical) and OS (recent holdout) periods. OS Sharpe is often lower than IS — a significant drop (>40%) suggests overfitting.

is_period.note: The exact split updates periodically as Brain extends its historical database.

os_period.note: OS is the forward-looking holdout. A healthy alpha shows IS Sharpe ≈ OS Sharpe (within 30%).

in_sample_out_of_sample.overfitting_signal: IS Sharpe >> OS Sharpe suggests the signal is data-mined. Prefer simpler expressions with fewer parameters.

SELF_CORRELATION.description: Pairwise PnL correlation with your OWN previously submitted alphas in your pool.
SELF_CORRELATION.meaning: Fail if this alpha's daily PnL is correlated >70% with any alpha you already submitted. Prevents submitting the same alpha twice under different names.
SELF_CORRELATION.fix: Change the signal significantly — different fields, different time horizon, or different archetype.

PROD_CORRELATION.description: Correlation with the Brain platform's production alpha book (all other users' submitted alphas).
PROD_CORRELATION.meaning: Fail if this alpha is too similar to what others are already trading. Encourages unique signals.
PROD_CORRELATION.fix: Explore less-saturated archetypes (e.g., options_implied, dispersion) or unusual field combinations.

CONCENTRATED_WEIGHT.description: Checks if the portfolio is over-concentrated in a small number of stocks.
CONCENTRATED_WEIGHT.typical_limit: Top stock weight > some threshold of total book (exact limit varies)
CONCENTRATED_WEIGHT.fix: Lower truncation (e.g., from 0.10 to 0.05), or use rank()/zscore() to spread weights more evenly.

delay_1.description: Trade at NEXT DAY's open/close using data available as of today's market close.
delay_1.data_available: All fundamentals, analyst estimates, earnings data, options IV, all price/volume fields. Full field catalog.
delay_1.use_when: Default for all non-intraday signals. Fundamental ratios, analyst revisions, earnings event — all need delay=1.

delay_0.description: Trade at TODAY's close using data available within today's trading session.
delay_0.data_available: ONLY intraday price/volume (close, open, high, low, vwap, volume, returns), options IV, and a subset of vector sentiment fields. Most fundamentals are NOT available at delay=0.
delay_0.use_when: Intraday signals only: close-vs-VWAP divergence, intraday range, options skew on the same day.
delay_0.warning: Avoid using fundamental fields at delay=0 — they will either be unavailable or use stale values from the prior day.
delay_0.typical_settings: Higher decay (10–15) recommended for delay=0 to avoid over-churn from daily re-evaluation.

expression_evaluation.execution_model: Cross-sectional: evaluated ONCE per stock per day. No loops, no time-series accumulation in user code — use ts_* operators for any rolling window logic.
expression_evaluation.scalar_output: Expression must produce one scalar per stock per day. Vectors, matrices, or multi-dimensional outputs are invalid.
expression_evaluation.sign_convention: Positive value → LONG position. Negative value → SHORT position. Zero → no position.
expression_evaluation.forbidden_side_effects: Expressions are stateless — no global state, no file I/O, no randomness. Pure mathematical functions only.

operator_semantics.ts_mean(x, d): Trailing d-day equal-weighted mean of x. d must be an integer >= 1.
operator_semantics.ts_std_dev(x, d): Trailing d-day standard deviation. Uses N-1 denominator (sample std).
operator_semantics.ts_delta(x, d): x[today] - x[d days ago]. NOT percentage change — if you want return-like, divide by x[d days ago] or ts_mean(x, d).
operator_semantics.ts_corr(x, y, d): Trailing d-day Pearson correlation between x and y. Returns values in [-1, 1].
operator_semantics.ts_rank(x, d): Rank of today's x value within its trailing d-day window. Returns a value in [1/d, 1]. Useful as an ordinal replacement for ts_max/ts_min.
operator_semantics.ts_zscore(x, d): Z-score of today's x relative to its trailing d-day mean and std: (x - ts_mean(x,d)) / ts_std_dev(x,d).
operator_semantics.ts_decay_linear(x, d): Linearly weighted moving average: weights decrease from d (most recent) to 1 (d days ago), then normalized. Different from the settings-level decay (which is exponential).
operator_semantics.rank(x): Cross-sectional rank across the current universe. Returns uniform [0,1] distribution — very robust to outliers.
operator_semantics.zscore(x): Cross-sectional z-score across the current universe. Sensitive to outliers — use rank() if fields have heavy tails.
operator_semantics.group_neutralize(x, sector): Subtract sector mean from x within each sector. Set settings.neutralization=Market when using this to avoid double-demeaning.
operator_semantics.signed_power(x, e): x * |x|^(e-1). Preserves sign. Use instead of pow(x, e) when x can be negative.

common_design_rules.always_normalize_price: Raw price (close, open, high, low, vwap) is dollar-dominated — mega-caps dominate. Always ratio-normalize: close/ts_mean(close, N) or ts_delta(close, 1)/close.
common_design_rules.always_normalize_volume: Raw volume is share-count dominated — don't use ts_sum(volume, 5) alone. Use ts_sum(volume, 5)/ts_mean(volume, 60) for volume surge.
common_design_rules.turnover_budget: Target 5–35% daily turnover for best fitness. Short windows (<5 days) drive high turnover. For reversal: 10–20 days. For fundamental: 63–252 days.
common_design_rules.negate_lottery: Mean of (returns)^3 is the cubic moment — high value = lottery-like. ALWAYS negate it: -ts_mean(r^3, 21) to short lottery stocks, which is the empirically profitable direction.
common_design_rules.rank_before_combining: When multiplying two signals, rank() each first to prevent one signal dominating due to scale: rank(signal_A) * rank(signal_B).
common_design_rules.avoid_overfitting: Expressions with more than 3-4 parameters are likely overfit. Prefer economically motivated single-mechanism alphas.
